name: Stockport to Manchester Piccadilly
note: Corridor waypoints and station positions from an OpenStreetMap export (tools/osm-to-network.mjs, 8 October 2026): the shortest rail path from Davenport to Piccadilly, resampled every 60 m, on one track of the four-track line, with the Hazel Grove line (11 October 2026, the same way) put in front of it, and the Buxton line in front of that (13 October 2026: OpenStreetMap's main API, the shortest rail path from Whaley Bridge to Hazel Grove, every 60 m, on the track away from Manchester, from 630 m beyond New Mills Newtown, so the line runs on past the last platform; it replaces the 150 m beyond Hazel Grove the first export drew along the Hazel Grove Chord, and its start is placed so the line gains a whole number of signal sections, 8,800 m, and every distance and signal on today's line moves by exactly that); cut into two corridors at Edgeley Junction (13 October 2026, `corridorNote`). Landmarks are still by hand. Each station's access (its car park's and bus link's pools beyond a walk) is from tools/census-to-network.mjs (12 October 2026): straight-line distances from Census 2021 Output Areas times a road factor of 1.3, at 8 m/s driving and 5 m/s by bus, half of each area's residents driving and half by bus (docs/DESIGN.md, Homes and draw, Pools); the car parks' spaces and the stages' prices are game choices.

The Rose Hill branch, from beyond Rose Hill to Marple Wharf Junction

The Macclesfield leg, from beyond Poynton to Cheadle Hulme North Junction (through Bramhall)

corridorNote: Each corridor is one real line's centreline, drawn towards Manchester, so distances along every one of them grow towards Piccadilly. The OpenStreetMap path the line was first drawn from is cut at Edgeley Junction: the Hazel Grove line runs up to it and the line to Piccadilly on from it. Each corridor's waypoints run a couple past the junction it starts or ends at, so its curve there is the same as the uncut line's, and it's cut at the junction's point (`from`, `to`). Distances along the line (chainage) run on through the junctions: from 0 at the start of the spine (the corridors the ground is laid along, end to end), and along any other corridor so they meet the line it joins at the junction's own chainage.

junctions.name: Edgeley Junction
junctions.note: Where the Hazel Grove (Buxton) line leaves the line to Crewe and curves sharply east: Wikipedia (Buxton line, read 13 October 2026) puts it half a mile south of Stockport, and the corridor from OpenStreetMap starts its curve east here, 1000 m south of the station's middle (785 m south of its platforms), where the four main lines already began. Edgeley Junction No. 2, where the Mid-Cheshire line leaves westwards, is close by (from memory); the Crewe line goes on south from here.

junctions.name: Heaton Norris Junction
junctions.note: Just north of the viaduct, where the Stockport to Stalybridge line (Reddish South and Denton) leaves eastwards: from memory, placed where the OpenStreetMap tracks cross over north of the viaduct (the layout note), the junction's own crossovers.

junctions.name: Slade Lane Junction
junctions.note: In Longsight, where the Styal line leaves southwards for Manchester Airport and Wilmslow (Wikipedia, Styal line, read 13 October 2026): placed where the OpenStreetMap tracks part (the layout note), 600 m north of Levenshulme.

junctions.name: Ardwick Junction
junctions.note: West of Ardwick station, where the lines to Ashburys (the Hope Valley line through Reddish North to Marple and Rose Hill, and the Glossop line) leave the line to Longsight: OpenStreetMap's Ardwick Junction (the main API, 13 October 2026), 220 m north of the game's Ardwick platforms, placed on the corridor 14.5 m west of it (OpenStreetMap has it on the east track). The Hope Valley lines run on beside the Longsight lines on their east side into Piccadilly's platforms 1 to 4 (OpenStreetMap, 14 October 2026), as the game's Marple pair does from here (`hope-valley-north` and `hope-valley-south`).

junctions.name: Marple Wharf Junction
junctions.note: Where the Rose Hill branch (the old Macclesfield, Bollington and Marple line) leaves the Marple line south-westwards, 1 km south of Romiley by the Peak Forest Canal: OpenStreetMap's Marple Wharf Junction (the main API, 13 October 2026), where their tracks meet, placed 60 m north of it on the Marple line's corridor, where the branch's track has come alongside, so its two ways part there. Romiley Junction, just north of Romiley, where the line from Woodley and Hyde joins, isn't marked: no line comes in there yet.

junctions.name: Cheadle Hulme North Junction
junctions.note: Where the Macclesfield line (through Bramhall and Poynton, on to Stoke) leaves the Crewe line south-eastwards, just north of Cheadle Hulme station, whose platforms 3 and 4 are on the Macclesfield line and 1 and 2 on the Crewe line: OpenStreetMap's Cheadle Hulme North Junction (spelt Cheadie in its name; the main API, 14 October 2026).

junctions.name: Wilmslow South Junction
junctions.note: Where the Styal line (from Manchester Airport) joins the Crewe line, just south of Wilmslow station, after running beside it through the station's own platforms: OpenStreetMap's Wilmslow South Junction (the main API, 14 October 2026). No line comes in here yet; the Styal line is next.

junctionNote: Junctions are named points on a corridor where other corridors start or end; the ones with no line beyond them yet are where the lines out of Stockport and Manchester will join (docs/ROADMAP.md, phase 5).

trackNote: Offsets are where each track runs across the corridor, at the real spacing from the OpenStreetMap tracks (13 October 2026: until then 1.25 times real, with the trains drawn 1.3 times real width; every offset here was divided by 1.25, and the trains drawn at their real width pass clear of each other). On the open line the corridor follows the westmost track. The layout list moves the tracks where the corridor follows another track and around the stations; they ease between layouts over `ease` metres.

layout.note: Stockport's tracks, from OpenStreetMap (13 October 2026) and narrowed towards real widths so the throats fit: west to east, the down slow at platform 4, the down fast at 3 and the up fast at 2 between the two islands, the up slow at 1 with the Hazel Grove line, and platform 0's bay. Each holds its platform's line from the south end of the platforms to u = 120, where they now end, and fans in to its place on the viaduct by u = 280 to 390, at no more than 1 in 5 (docs/DESIGN.md, Where the tracks run); the viaduct's deck is drawn as wide as the tracks on it, as the real one carries the throat on its first spans. Each track has its own entry, so each eases over its own length. A stopper turning in 4 or 3 crosses over to its track north of the throat.

The Hazel Grove line runs east of the main lines from Edgeley Junction (where the Buxton line leaves eastwards), fans out beside the up slow and merges into platform 1 over the last 70 m before the platforms.

Beyond Hazel Grove the corridor follows the line's eastern track, the one away from Manchester (OpenStreetMap, 13 October 2026), as it does through Hazel Grove, so the tracks hold that layout all the way out.
Coming up to Edgeley Junction the Hazel Grove line moves east of where the main lines begin, as it joins them on their east side.
From the crossover north of the viaduct to Slade Lane junction the corridor follows the second track from the west. Heaton Chapel and Levenshulme are in this stretch.
Through Hazel Grove the corridor follows the eastern track; it crosses to the western one north of the platforms.

Piccadilly's tracks, from OpenStreetMap (14 October 2026): the four Longsight lines (the main lines from Stockport) run into platform 5 and the bays 6 to 12 west of it, as the real ones run into 5 to 12, and the two Hope Valley lines from Ardwick Junction into 1 to 4 on the north side. The Longsight lines close up into one road with the down slow from u = -880 to -775 (a game choice: the real throat is a ladder of crossovers there), so every train from Stockport runs on into platform 5 or the bays' lead, which leaves the down slow westwards from u = -880, where an express for a bay crosses over from the fast line to it, on the arches as on the real line, each bay peeling off it at 1 in 6.5 to its platform's line, as OpenStreetMap's west throat fans. The Hope Valley line towards Manchester holds its offset into platform 3, east of them all; the line out of platform 2 eases over from u = -580 to -360, clear of the islands, and platform 4 leaves the first westwards and platform 1 the second eastwards. A train for a platform off its own track crosses over beyond the throat, on a crossover drawn with its rails (docs/DESIGN.md, Where the tracks run).

Coming up to Ardwick Junction the Marple line's pair runs on beside the Longsight lines on their east side as the Hope Valley lines (OpenStreetMap, the main API, 14 October 2026: 3.9 m east of the up slow and 3.4 m apart), into Piccadilly's platforms 1 to 4.

The branch is a single line (OpenStreetMap, 13 October 2026), so both its tracks are the one road; at Marple Wharf Junction it parts to meet both Marple lines, the line towards Rose Hill crossing the one towards Manchester on the flat.

Coming up to Edgeley Junction the Crewe line's two tracks spread to meet the line to Piccadilly's slow lines, the line towards Manchester running into the down slow and the line towards Crewe out of the up slow, the two straddling the fast lines as the Marple line's do at Ardwick Junction. The corridor (OpenStreetMap's Crewe line, the main API, 14 October 2026) comes in from the south-south-west at about 35 degrees to the line to Piccadilly's start, so the up slow's end is drawn about 6 m along from the Crewe line's (handed on).

At Cheadle Hulme North Junction the Macclesfield line's tracks run into the Crewe line's own: its corridor (OpenStreetMap, 14 October 2026) follows the line's track towards Manchester, 1.5 m west of the Crewe line's at the junction.

landmarks.name: Stockport Viaduct
landmarks.note: 27 arches on tall piers, about 34 m over the Mersey, red brick; built 1839-40 by George Watson Buck and widened on its west side to four tracks in 1887-89, the join showing down the soffits (geograph 1073460, 8038086; Commons: Category:Stockport Viaduct). Floodlit at night. Its span along the line is where the Environment Agency's LIDAR has the ground fall away beneath it (tools/lidar-to-terrain.mjs).

landmarks.name: The arches into Piccadilly
landmarks.note: The line from beyond Ardwick's platforms to Piccadilly's throat runs on brick arches over the streets of Ardwick (Wikipedia, Manchester Piccadilly station: the approach on a viaduct; the LIDAR has the ground 5 to 11 m below the rail all the way); its ends are where the two stations' land begins, about 10 m spans from memory. Piccadilly's own throat and undercroft stand on the station's land.

landmarks.name: River Mersey
landmarks.note: Where the LIDAR has the valley floor lowest under the viaduct. Its course (`course`, west to east) traced along the valley floor in the LIDAR base and fine tiles from here both ways, 12 October 2026: west past Brinksway, and east under Merseyway; its last stretch, below the Market Place's bluff to where the Tame and the Goyt meet by Lancashire Bridge (where the Mersey begins: Wikipedia, River Mersey), from memory, since the trace climbs the Goyt there; and kept north of the Plaza, where the real river runs culverted under Mersey Square; OpenStreetMap was still blocked.

landmarks.name: M60
landmarks.note: Where the LIDAR has the motorway's level stretch under the viaduct, north of the river. Its course (`course`, west to east) from memory, checked against the LIDAR's level: along the valley's north side west of the viaduct past the Pyramid and junction 1, then north-east after the viaduct past Lancashire Hill towards junction 27 at Portwood (Wikipedia, M60 motorway); OpenStreetMap was still blocked.

landmarks.name: Stockport Pyramid
landmarks.note: Steel-framed blue glass pyramid of 1987-92 by Michael Hyde and Associates, beside the M60 at Brinksway (geograph 2350452, 3116288; Commons: Category:Stockport Pyramid gives 53.408, -2.1754). At the real spot; its size from the photos, not survey.

landmarks.name: The Plaza
landmarks.note: The 1932 art deco super cinema on Mersey Square: a tall cream faience front with a stepped centre and its name down a fin, built into the sandstone cliff (geograph 1974759, 5194359). At its real spot (the middle of its outline in OpenStreetMap, way 274262844, main API, 14 October 2026), facing the river. Proportions from the photos.

landmarks.name: Merseyway
landmarks.note: The 1960s shopping precinct built on a deck over the River Mersey, two runs of shops either side of the walk (geograph 7305032, 8287347; at its real spot, about 53.4114, -2.1600). Stands on the river's course as the map draws it, at its real spot, between the viaduct and the A6's Wellington Bridge; the shops' sizes from memory.

landmarks.name: St Mary's Church

platformNote: Which platform each service uses (12 October 2026). The owner: trains from Stockport to Manchester use platforms 3 and 4, both of them. Wikipedia (Stockport railway station, Manchester Piccadilly station, read 12 October 2026): at Stockport platform 4 is the northbound stoppers', 3 the northbound main-line trains (Avanti West Coast, 3 an hour, and CrossCountry, 2 an hour, to Piccadilly), 2 the southbound main-line trains (to London, Bristol and Bournemouth), 1 southbound stoppers and signalled for trains to Manchester, 0 southbound towards Hazel Grove and Buxton, 3a the weekly train to Stalybridge; at Piccadilly platform 1 is on the north side (the kit's +v) and 13 and 14 on the south, 5 to 9 are the longest and mostly Avanti's and CrossCountry's, 10 to 12 shorter, for local trains including the Buxton line. Game choices: the stopper turns at Stockport in 4, 3 and the bay 0, and at Piccadilly in 5, 11 and 12, each unit its own first choice so every platform built has trains; the Hazel Grove line turns in Stockport's 1; the expresses use 3 north and 2 south at Stockport (running through until those are built) and 6 and 7 at Piccadilly (5 while the player owns it without the shed). The Marple and Rose Hill trains (13 October 2026) turn at Piccadilly in 1 to 4, on the north side where the real Hope Valley trains go, on their own pair from Ardwick Junction (14 October 2026), once Piccadilly's platforms are built, and before that in 5 beside the stopper (a game choice). A through station's platforms are the halt's (1) and the second platform (2), which aren't their real numbers everywhere. The expresses' destinations south: Avanti's London Euston, CrossCountry's Bristol Temple Meads (some go to Bournemouth); one of each every two clock hours, Avanti's from 06:30 to 22:30 and CrossCountry's from 07:30 to 21:30 as they come on south of Stockport (`first`, `every` and `last` in `through`, clock hours): not their real frequency, which the clock running six to twelve times faster than the trains would make a train every few minutes, but their real day, the first about 06:00 and the last about 23:00 (Wikipedia's timetable notes), so the night is quiet.

frequency.note: Northern's stoppers through Heaton Chapel and Levenshulme (to Alderley Edge and Crewe), two an hour off-peak and three in the peaks (Wikipedia, Heaton Chapel and Levenshulme stations, read 14 October 2026; the peaks' third from memory): a real train an hour is one and a half units here, as the stopper's three units are its real two an hour (a game choice: the clock runs six to sixty times faster than the trains, so the real frequency on the clock would be a train every few minutes). Its peak unit rests in Stockport's carriage sidings between the peaks.

manchester.note: Northern's Buxton and Hazel Grove trains run through Stockport to Piccadilly, calling at Heaton Chapel and Levenshulme but not Ardwick (Wikipedia, Buxton line, Heaton Chapel and Levenshulme stations, read 14 October 2026), so once bought these do: through Stockport's platform 1 both ways, where trains for Manchester are signalled too (Wikipedia, Stockport station), crossing over to the down slow north of the throat and back off the up slow, and turning at Piccadilly in 12 or 11, where the real Buxton line's go (5 before Piccadilly's platforms stage). Its units then run out from Piccadilly and stand overnight at the far end, and a peak unit rests at Piccadilly between the peaks. Offered once Piccadilly's train shed and bays are built, since with the halt's one platform there the stoppers, the Marple trains and these would all queue for 5 (a game choice).

services.name: TransPennine Express
services.note: TransPennine Express's Cleethorpes trains (14 October 2026): off the Hope Valley line by the Hazel Grove chord, which joins the Buxton line south-east of Hazel Grove (from memory: placed 700 m beyond the station), through Davenport and Woodsmoor without stopping, calling at Stockport in platform 1 both ways (the Hazel Grove line's road in; the real ones use whichever is free) and on to Piccadilly on the fast lines. The real ones run on through platforms 13 and 14 to Liverpool; here they turn in the bays 7 and 6 with the other expresses (the shorter bays' buffers stand too close for the front of a turning express), as 13 and 14 aren't in service (a game choice). One every four clock hours, 06:00 to 22:00: the real ones are hourly, a third of Avanti's three an hour, as the game's every two hours is Avanti's (a game choice, as for the other expresses).

services.name: Marple line
services.note: Out from Piccadilly along the Marple line as far as stations are owned, from Ashburys (13 October 2026): Northern's stoppers to Marple and on to New Mills Central and Sheffield, about two an hour between them, call at every station from Ashburys to Marple except some at Belle Vue and Ryder Brow, which have fewer; here every train calls at every owned station, and one unit runs it however far it reaches, turning at the furthest owned station (game choices: the real ones run on beyond Marple, step 4 for through running). From Ardwick Junction it runs on its own pair into Piccadilly, as the real Hope Valley lines do (14 October 2026), and turns in platforms 1 to 4, the north side's, where the real Hope Valley and Marple trains go (Wikipedia, Manchester Piccadilly station), once Piccadilly's platforms are built; before that, in the stopper's 5 (a game choice).

frequency.note: Northern's Marple trains, two an hour (one to New Mills Central, one to Sheffield) and more in the peaks (Wikipedia, Marple station, read 14 October 2026; the peaks' extra from memory): a real train an hour is one and a half units here, as the stopper's three units are its real two an hour (a game choice: the clock runs six to sixty times faster than the trains, so the real frequency on the clock would be a train every few minutes). Its peak unit rests on the roads through platforms 13 and 14 at Piccadilly between the peaks (a game choice: those platforms aren't in service yet).

roadNote: Roads between neighbouring stations, for the rail replacement buses (and later trams and buses), every one from OpenStreetMap's main API by tools/osm-to-roads.mjs (13 and 14 October 2026; the first were from memory): the quickest way by road, keeping to the main roads, mostly the A6, which runs beside the line all the way, with the side streets to each station's stop, resampled every 40 m.
